rules.statement: When the caller can't know the output size ahead of time, an API that writes variable-length output takes an IBufferWriter<byte> destination instead of a fixed Memory<byte>/Span<byte> destination; keep Span plus an `out int` bytes-written only for results whose size is known in advance.
rules.why: Callers who can't know the size end up guessing a buffer size, for example renting twice the expected length. That hides real errors as "destination too small" or pushes them into later size checks.
rules.check: Look for new or changed methods that write to a caller-supplied Memory<byte>/Span<byte> where the output length is only known after the work is done (for example a remote service response or a decryption result). Also look for callers that over-rent buffers to guess the size.
